choices.text: Nothing: two things changed

choices.text: Prose is harmless, since the difference looks like chance

prompt: Why does `pl compare` line up the two results of each message instead of comparing two totals?

choices.text: Nothing: anything above 0.05 means no effect
choices.why: 0.05 is a line people agreed on, not a threshold of reality.

choices.text: Not shown is not none

prompt: What does a small p on a comparison tell you?

choices.text: The probability that the change helped
choices.why: That is the most common misreading.

choices.text: That the change caused the difference
choices.why: It says the split is unlikely by chance, not what caused it.

choices.text: The split is unlikely by chance
choices.why: Right: and nothing about which change, if several rode along.

choices.text: That the new prompt is better
choices.why: It could be worse; p is about the split, either way.
